Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 94, verses 1–8:

It is a Meccan surah without any disagreement.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "Alam nashrah was revealed in Mecca," and he added: "after the forenoon (al-duha)."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAʾishah that she said: "The surah Alam nashrah was revealed in Mecca."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The meaning of sharh al-sadr (expansion of the breast) is opening it by removing whatever blocks understanding. When the interrogative (istifham) enters upon a negation, it affirms it, so the meaning becomes: "Indeed, We have expanded your breast for you." He specified the breast because it is the locus of the states of the soul, such as knowledge and perceptions. The intent is to bestow favour upon him (ﷺ) by opening and widening his breast, until he was able to carry out the call he made, and was capable of what he was capable of, bearing the burdens of prophethood and preserving the revelation. This matter has already been discussed at the explanation of His words: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord?﴾ [al-Zumar: 22].

﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾ is coordinated (maʿtuf) upon the meaning of what preceded, not upon its wording: i.e., "We have expanded your breast for you and We removed..." From this is the saying of Jarir praising ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan:

"Are you not the best of those who have ridden the mounts, and the most generous of the people of the world in giving wine?"
i.e., "You are the best of those who have ridden the mounts, and the most generous, etc."

The majority (al-Jumhur) read nashrah with the letter ḥāʾ vowelled by sukun (jazm). Abu Jaʿfar al-Mansur al-ʿAbbasi read it with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ.

al-Zamakhshari said: "They said: perhaps he articulated the ḥāʾ, prolonging it in its place of articulation, so the listener thought he had put a fatḥah on it."

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: the original is "alam nashraḥan" with the light nūn, then it was changed into an alif, then it was deleted for lightness, as Abu Zayd recited:

"From which of my two days of death do I flee: a day not decreed, or a day decreed?"
with a fatḥah on the rāʾ in "lam yuqaddar." Similar to this is his saying:

"Strike away from you the worries that come at night, with a strike of the sword on the forehead of the horse,"
with a fatḥah on the bāʾ of "iḍrib." This is based on permitting the apocopated (majzum) verb to be emphasized with lam, which is very rare, like his saying:

"The ignorant man thinks he does not know, an old man upon his chair, turbaned."

Thus this reading is composed of three principles, all of which are weak. The first is emphasizing the apocopated verb with lam, which is weak. The second is changing it into an alif, which is specific to pausal form (waqf), so treating the continuous recitation as pausal is weak. The third is deleting the alif, which is also weak, because it contradicts the original form. Some have explained it according to the dialect of some Arabs who put the verb in the accusative after lam and apocopate it after lan. From this is the saying of the poet:

(p-1635) "In every matter he sought, he pursued his opinion boldly, and did not consult anyone in his undertaking,"
with a fatḥah on the rāʾ of "yushawir." I do not think this dialect is sound; and even if it were sound, it is not among the recognised dialects, for it comes contrary to what the whole of the Arabic language follows.

In any case, the reading of this man, despite his extreme tyranny, great oppression, abundant arrogance and little knowledge, is not worthy of being occupied with.

Al-wizr means sin: i.e., "We removed from you what you were in of the matter of jahiliyyah."

al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: the meaning is "We lowered from you what had passed of you in the jahiliyyah." This is like His saying: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2].

﴿The one who weighed down your back﴾ — the exegetes said: i.e., made your back heavy.

al-Zajjaj said: he made it so heavy that a creaking (naqīḍ), i.e., a sound, was heard from it. This is similar in meaning to: that if it were a load being carried, the creaking of your back would be heard. The people of the language say: "The load creaked the she-camel's back" when a grinding sound was heard from it. From this is the saying of Jamil:

"Until its ropes creaked with a sound, and the joints of its back were about to break,"

and the saying of al-ʿAbbas ibn Mirdas:

"And the weight of what I bore from them creaked my back, and I was concerned for them, compassionate."

Qatadah said: the Prophet (ﷺ) had sins that weighed him down, and Allah forgave them. Others hold that this refers to the lightening of the burdens of prophethood, which weigh down the back in carrying out its matters; Allah made that easy for him until it became manageable for him. Abu ʿUbaydah and others also said so. Ibn Masʿud read: "And We unloaded from you your burden (wiqrak)."

Then He (glorified is He) mentioned His favour upon him and His honour, saying: ﴿And We raised high your mention﴾. al-Hasan said: this is because Allah is not mentioned in any place without the Prophet (ﷺ) being mentioned with Him.

Qatadah said: Allah raised his mention in this world and the Hereafter; there is no preacher, no one reciting the tashahhud, and no one performing prayer, except that they call out, saying: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Mujahid said: "And We raised high your mention" means by the adhan (call to prayer).

It has also been said: the meaning is that We mentioned you in the books revealed to the prophets before him, and commanded them to give glad tidings of him; and it has been said: We raised your mention among the angels in the heavens and among the believers on earth.

The apparent meaning is that this raising of his mention, by which Allah bestowed favour upon him, encompasses all of these matters, so each of them is one of the causes of raising his mention. Likewise His command to send blessings and peace upon him, and his (ﷺ) report from Allah, mighty and majestic, that whoever sends blessings upon him once, Allah sends blessings upon him ten times for it; and Allah's command to obey him, as in His saying: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Nur: 54], His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7], His saying: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al ʿImran: 31], and other than these.

In sum, his glorious mention has filled the heavens and the earth, and Allah has given him a tongue of truth, a good remembrance and a righteous praise, such as He has not given to any of His servants. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Hadid: 21]. O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him and upon his family, as many times as those who pray upon him have prayed, in every tongue, in every age. How beautiful is the saying of Hassan:

"Radiant, upon him is the seal of prophethood, a sign from Allah, famous, shining and witnessing,"

"Allah joined the name of the Prophet with His own name, when the muezzin says in the five (prayers): I bear witness,"

"And He derived for Him a name from His own, to honour him: the Lord of the Throne is Mahmud, and this is Muhammad."

﴿So indeed with hardship is ease﴾ — i.e., with narrowness is expansiveness, with severity is relief, with distress is relief.

In this is a promise from Him (glorified is He) that every difficulty will be made easy, every severity will become light, and every hardship will become soft.

Then He (glorified is He) increased this promise in confirmation and emphasis, saying, repeating it with the words ﴿Indeed with hardship is ease﴾: i.e., indeed with that hardship mentioned previously is another ease, because it is established that when a definite noun is repeated, the second is the same as the first, whether the intended meaning is the genus or a specific reference; unlike an indefinite noun, when repeated, where the second generally refers to a different individual from the first. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said regarding the meaning of this verse: "Hardship will never overcome two eases." al-Wahidi said: this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), the Companions and the exegetes, that hardship is one and ease is two.

al-Zajjaj said: He mentioned hardship with the definite article, then repeated its mention, so the meaning becomes: indeed with hardship are two eases.

It has been said that the indefiniteness of "ease" is for magnification and exaltation. In the codex of Ibn Masʿud it is not repeated.

The majority read the sin in ʿusr and yusr in both places with sukun. Yahya ibn Wathhab, Abu Jaʿfar and ʿIsa read them with a ḍammah throughout.

﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — i.e., when you have finished your prayer, or from conveying the message, or from the raid, then labour: i.e., strive in supplication and ask Allah for your need; or labour in worship. Al-nasab means fatigue; it is said: "nasiba yansabu nasaban," meaning he became tired.

Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: when you have finished the obligatory prayer, then labour toward your Lord in supplication, and turn to Him in asking, and He will give you. Mujahid also said likewise.

al-Shaʿbi said: when you have finished conveying the message, then labour: i.e., seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and women.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: when you have finished fighting your enemy, then labour in the worship of your Lord.

Mujahid also said: when you have finished with your worldly affairs, then labour in your prayer.

﴿And to your Lord turn with desire﴾ — al-Zajjaj said: i.e., make your desire directed to Allah alone.

ʿAta said: he means that he humbles himself before Him, fearing the Fire and longing for Paradise. The meaning is that he turns with desire to Him (glorified is He) and to no other, whoever that may be; so he seeks his needs from Him alone, and relies in all his affairs upon Him alone.

The majority read "fa-irghab." Zayd ibn ʿAli and Ibn Abi ʿAbalah read "fa-raghghib" with a shaddah on the ghayn: i.e., make people desire Allah and yearn for them toward what He has of good.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you?﴾ He said: Allah expanded his breast for Islam.

Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Jibril came to me and said: Your Lord says: Do you know how I raised your mention? I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with Me."

The chain of Ibn Jarir is thus: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid.

Abu Yaʿla narrated it through the route of Ibn Lahiʿah from Darraj.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through the route of Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla with it.

So Allah revealed: ﴿So indeed with hardship is ease. Indeed with hardship is ease.﴾" The wording of al-Tabarani is: "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿So indeed with hardship is ease. Indeed with hardship is ease.﴾"

al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, likewise as a marfuʿ report, something similar. al-Suyuti said: its chain is weak.

Indeed with hardship is ease.﴾" al-Bazzar said: we do not know of anyone who narrated it from Anas except ʿA'idh ibn Shurayh. Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him in his narrations: there is weakness; but Shuʿbah narrated it from Muʿawiyah ibn Qurrah from a man from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day joyful and happy, laughing, and saying: Hardship will never overcome two eases; indeed with hardship is ease, indeed with hardship is ease." This is a mursal report.

A similar report has been narrated as a marfuʿ mursal from Qatadah.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various routes from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — the verse — he said: When you are finished with the prayer, then labour in supplication, ask Allah, and turn to Him with desire.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him: Allah said to His Messenger: When you are finished with the prayer and have recited the tashahhud, then labour toward your Lord and ask Him for your need.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in al-Dhikr from Ibn Masʿud: ﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — toward supplication — ﴿And to your Lord turn with desire﴾ — in asking.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: ﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — he said: When you are free from the obligatory duties, then labour in the night prayer.

The majority read "fa-irghab." Zayd ibn ʿAli and Ibn Abi ʿAbalah read "fa-raghghib" with a shaddah on the ghayn: i.e., make people desire Allah and yearn for them toward what He has of good.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you?﴾ He said: Allah expanded his breast for Islam.

Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Jibril came to me and said: Your Lord says: Do you know how I raised your mention? I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with Me."

The chain of Ibn Jarir is thus: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid.

Abu Yaʿla narrated it through the route of Ibn Lahiʿah from Darraj.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through the route of Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla with it.

Ibn ʿAsakir narrated through the route of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And We raised high your mention﴾ — the verse — he said: Allah is not mentioned except that he is mentioned with Him.

al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab narrated from Anas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting and in front of him was a hole, and he said: If hardship entered this hole, ease would come until it entered upon it and brought it out. So Allah revealed: ﴿So indeed with hardship is ease. Indeed with hardship is ease.﴾" The wording of al-Tabarani is: "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿So indeed with hardship is ease. Indeed with hardship is ease.﴾"

Ibn al-Najjar narrated from him similar to it, as a marfuʿ report.

al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, likewise as a marfuʿ report, something similar. al-Suyuti said: its chain is weak.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Sabr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab narrated from Ibn Masʿud, as a marfuʿ report: "If hardship were in a hole, ease would follow it until it entered into it and brought it out. And hardship will never overcome two eases. Indeed Allah says: ﴿So indeed with hardship is ease. Indeed with hardship is ease.﴾" al-Bazzar said: we do not know of anyone who narrated it from Anas except ʿA'idh ibn Shurayh. Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him in his narrations: there is weakness; but Shuʿbah narrated it from Muʿawiyah ibn Qurrah from a man from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day joyful and happy, laughing, and saying: Hardship will never overcome two eases; indeed with hardship is ease, indeed with hardship is ease." This is a mursal report.

A similar report has been narrated as a marfuʿ mursal from Qatadah.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various routes from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — the verse — he said: When you are finished with the prayer, then labour in supplication, ask Allah, and turn to Him with desire.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him: Allah said to His Messenger: When you are finished with the prayer and have recited the tashahhud, then labour toward your Lord and ask Him for your need.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in al-Dhikr from Ibn Masʿud: ﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — toward supplication — ﴿And to your Lord turn with desire﴾ — in asking.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: ﴿So when you are free, then labour﴾ — he said: When you are free from the obligatory duties, then labour in the night prayer.
